label: Concurrent actualization typed: the crux of the existential-inertia dispute over immensity
summary: Follow-up to attempt c94eed5b, next test 1. Module TruthCore.Causality.ConcurrentActualization, spec specs/concurrent-actualization.toml. TYPED CRUX. Concurrent actualization (40a97664, weak): in every history, whatever has its esse received in some principle (EsseReceivedIn, DEF-ESSE-RECEIVED-IN: receiving potency to received act, the act/potency sense of 'not its own being') is given being (#1493 primitive GivesAt) by something at every moment at which it is present. Strong version 76d2cc96: by something distinct from it (excludes the thing's own persistence power, the form of the reply attributed to Feser 2021); registered strength order, strict (Control part 2). Rejected vocabulary: the adopted InPotency x esse, because DEF-POTENCY makes potency exclude act in the same respect, so 'present (hence in act as to being, 140544c4) and in potency as to being' would be empty and the premise vacuous. Semantic grounding (module docstring, statement paraphrase): meaning (remaining in received act at a moment is an actualization then and needs an actual actualizer then; it fuses the actualization principle with the contested thesis that continuing in received act is, at each moment, a potency being actualized; a primitive 'actualized at t' to split them would be an unconstrained atom), examples (air lit only while the sun acts, q.104 a.1 co.; a held stone, time profile only), the inertialist's offered counterexamples (the persisting rock, the water in the glass: the rival account, not established cases), structure (per moment, for each t some giver; not one giver throughout; giver need not be a tenseless cause of being). DERIVATION RESULT. Concurrent actualization alone does NOT give the sustaining reading: it is a for-each-moment claim and the relay interpretation (Control part 3) satisfies even the strong version with no sustaining cause. One further premise is needed and suffices together with the existing reception bridge da72ae93 (already a premise of the unified Dei Filius route): concurrence of causes of being (d7f5a528): whatever causes another's being gives it being at every moment at which anything gives it being (the quantifier swap and identification). From da72ae93, 40a97664 and d7f5a528 the weak sustaining reading ce55210c follows (sustainingOfConcurrentActualization): every cause of ANOTHER thing's being is CAUSE_OF_BEING_2. The restriction to causes distinct from their effect is forced (da72ae93 is about causes distinct from the effect) and costs nothing downstream: the creator conjunct of IMMENSE_2 concerns only other beings. 23e04ae5 strengthens ce55210c (registered, strict by Control part 5); the two existing arguments that use 23e04ae5 (ffef89fd, 0681f64a) now record strong_version_needed (frozen Challenges). Composition: ce55210c with presence-in-act 140544c4 and contact c4661518 gives the presence step 9469ab62 (immense2PresentToAllOfAnothers, non-transcription), and with the narrowed bridge a3913182 gives 8bf775e9 (immenseSenseBridgeOfAnothersSustaining, a declared single-application transcription, as in 0681f64a), so the concurrent-actualization derivation reaches the root route. Controls (e6d48136): extrinsic existential inertia satisfies the reception bridge, concurrence, presence-in-act and contact and falsifies concurrent actualization and the conclusion (part 1: the inertia interpretation falsifies the new premise, as intended); an intrinsic persistence power satisfies the weak concurrent actualization and falsifies the strong version and concurrence (part 2); relay falsifies concurrence with strong concurrent actualization (part 3); without received esse the reception bridge fails (part 4); every premise of the derivation and of the presence composition is needed in one interpretation; all hold together nonvacuously (part 7). OBJECTION AND WARRANT AUDIT (Substantive Objection Standard, both directions; Schmid 2021 and Feser 2021 rematerialized and reread this round, paragraphs cited by incipit). (a) Existential inertia (Schmid, SCHMID-INERTIA-REPLY-3-ARTICLE). Target: concurrent actualization 40a97664 (so ce55210c and both immensity routes through it); among the derivation's premises it is the only one the inertia interpretation falsifies. Mechanism: the no-change explanation, paragraphs beginning 'For S to fail to exist at m' and 'Here, we seem to have': (i) S existed immediately before m, (ii) nothing causally induced its cessation, (iii) a change occurs only if some factor causally induces it; ceasing would be a change; so S exists at m, with no concurrent giver. Independent justification: (iii) is a causal principle the Thomist side also accepts for change, and the deduction is valid. What it establishes: persistence is derivable from facts that include no concurrent giver, which undercuts the explanatory-need warrant for concurrent actualization, i.e. Feser's conditional that without a sustaining cause nothing extrinsic accounts for persistence (Schmid's paragraph beginning 'This is false' targets exactly it). It does not show concurrent actualization false: the premise could hold although persistence is otherwise derivable. Classification: substantive undercutting objection and a rival framework (Control part 1), not an established counterexample; no case is on file of a received-esse thing persisting with no giver. Typed side note, not an objection: concurrent actualization with (iii) requires that a giver's ceasing to give count as a factor inducing cessation, which the Thomist can grant. (b) Feser's case for concurrent actualization (FESER-INERTIA-REPLY-2021-ARTICLE). (b1) Composition sub-argument, paragraphs beginning 'Rather, a critique' and 'But this simply ignores': the parts at t, considered just qua parts, are only potentially the whole at t, so 'some additional factor active at t' is needed, and what happened at t-1 is not sufficient. The first clause is independently motivated (the essence-existence distinction, paragraph beginning 'This is, of course, an argument Aquinas gives'; hylemorphic analysis, defended elsewhere and not read here). The step from it to a factor active at t is concurrent actualization applied to the composite. The extrinsic account grants that nothing intrinsic to the parts secures the whole at t. Against it, the only ground the article gives for the insufficiency of the past is that the potential at t must be actualized at t. Provisional analyst judgment: against the extrinsic no-change account this step presupposes concurrent actualization. It does not presuppose the sustaining conclusion as a whole, since concurrence and the reception bridge are separate premises. (b2) The 'if EIT is false, EET' argument, paragraph beginning 'This too is not correct', uses the premise that without a sustaining cause nothing extrinsic accounts for persistence, the premise Schmid's account contests. Feser's article (6 July 2021) predates Schmid's reply (7 July 2021), so no answer to that reply is on file. (b3) The telescope analogy, paragraph beginning '(Compare: If there is nothing intrinsic to me': specific difference: seeing a mile is an achievement beyond the agent's capacity that needs an enabling factor, while persistence on the rival account is the absence of change; whether persisting is like the first or the second is the crux, so the analogy presupposes the point. (b4) The essence argument and 'the reason contingent things are contingent' (paragraphs beginning 'This is, of course' and 'But this is quite absurd'): independently justified against intrinsic and necessity versions of inertia (P-EIT; primitive necessary inertia) and supportive of the received-esse antecedent; it does not by itself yield concurrent actualization against an extrinsic account, which does not say that essence entails persistence. (b5) The circularity argument, paragraphs beginning 'Now, an objection', 'I find this' and 'Another problem': independently justified against an intrinsic persistence power; in the typed setting it is an argument for the strong over the weak version (Control part 2), and given the weak version, concurrence is what a persistence power violates; it does not reach the extrinsic account (as c94eed5b judged). (c) Concurrence d7f5a528: no substantive objection identified for esse-giving. Lead with no evidential weight for esse: ordinary illumination admits a relay of sources (a room lit by a lamp, then by daylight with the lamp off); that is an established case of the time profile only, and whether causes of esse admit replacement is the open difference; the immensity route needs concurrence only for a cause of the being of everything else, and a restriction to such causes would avoid the lead (not formalized). The motivation from the first cause's concurrence in every action (q.105 a.5) is unread and not relied on. (d) Reception bridge da72ae93: unchanged; its recorded lead (no real essence-esse distinction, Suarez) would remove the antecedent of concurrent actualization for creatures, a different route out than inertia. WHERE THE DISPUTE RESTS. On this route the existential-inertia dispute over immensity sits exactly at concurrent actualization 40a97664, specifically at the thesis that continuing in received act is an actualization at each moment. On the material read, Feser's argument for it presupposes it against the extrinsic rival, and Schmid's account shows only that it is not needed to derive persistence; neither discharges its burden at that point. Overall provisional judgment: unresolved; nothing is established. Every new premise is OPEN and unattributed. Bearing on #1501: ce55210c is a second cross-term bridge CAUSING_AN_EFFECT_3 -> CAUSE_OF_BEING_2 (restricted to causes of another's being), named in prose like 23e04ae5; folding CAUSE_OF_BEING into c3c01e92 would need to cover it.
blocker: Not blocked. Next tests: (1) type Schmid's principle (iii) (a change occurs only if some factor causally induces it) and the dependence clause of 56989bd0 (the thing would not be at t without the giving), and test whether concurrent actualization follows from (iii) plus a typed 'ceasing on withdrawal' principle or whether concurrent actualization and inertia are a clean fork over (iii); (2) restrict concurrence d7f5a528 to causes of the being of everything else and recompose the immensity route with it; (3) read q.104 a.1 ad 1-4 and q.105 a.5 for concurrence and for an argument that continuing in received act is an actualization; (4) read Feser's ACPQ article 'Existential Inertia and the Five Ways' and Schmid's linked no-change document (both unread) for an independent argument on concurrent actualization against the extrinsic account.
